message:
Manager, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, my counts are enforceable operating limits, not illustrations.

In plain words one tonne means fifty small boxes filled over four mornings with a paper log and a crate fee that pays for washing and repairs. Reusing the total produce mass estimate (E49) for 1000 kg as 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) at 20 kg each within single-person lift guidance from the manual handling sources, staged as 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250 kg staged intake (E78) under the staged rule from the revised steady-load simulation (E28), moved one 600 by 400 mm crate at a time through the 900 mm single-leaf door from the Coolroom Buying Guide: Walk-In Refrigeration for Kitchens (E71) onto two rack rows with 25 mm gaps per ventilation guidance from the Cold Storage of Agricultural Products source, with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest produce sold first) paper tags plus twice-daily wall thermometer checks and a door log funded by the pay-per-crate model from The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) and affordability precedent from Preserving Harvests: Fresh Solutions to Food Loss in Kenya (E72). About fourteen adults by weight in a small bedroom volume so everyday scale holds, and any 51st crate or unstaged tonne is refused at the door because full-tonne 25.0 kWh from the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) cannot fit a solar day. My position on the tonne workflow is closed except Manager update.

In plain words eight quick daytime door openings with the plastic curtain closed is the energy number, more openings breaks cold without breaking any rule unless the tie is written. Reusing the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) at 0.17 kWh per day which supersedes door 0.44 kWh per day sensible-only from the door infiltration estimate (E57), my discipline of maximum 8 openings per day daytime, single-crate pass, strip curtain, early-morning intake from Designing Efficient Cold Storage: Key Factors and Cooling Loads (E51) is the same eight openings that set that 0.17 kWh door term inside the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111). I declare this as the operating limit with attendant crate log, so a ninth opening or propped door is a logged violation that triggers refusal of further intake that day.

In plain words mixed vegetables stay at one safe setting and a warm full load or a dark cloudy store is refused, not absorbed. Single mixed holding setpoint 5 degrees Celsius from Small-Scale Postharvest Handling Practices guidance tolerating chilling-sensitive crops per lowest-safe-temperature rule stages 250 kg per day with shade plus pre-cool discipline, and on low charge the Low-Voltage Disconnect (LVD, automatic battery protector that sheds load) plus attendant refusal sheds new warm intake and defers opening until the battery autonomy simulation (E95) recovers, because cloud at 30 percent sun still ends at 3.73 kWh only under staged discipline. Full 1000 kg warm at once and night loading are refused by rule and named as bench-test discipline, not margin.

My position is not ready on the proposal as a whole, because my tonne plus door plus refusal chain now ties to the 0.17 kWh door model from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) and 10.4 kWh electrical total from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111) pending Manager update superseding 13.2 kWh per day and joint confirmation with Solar Energy Systems Engineer and Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer.
